slides.0.title: Principles of distillation and maturation
slides.0.subtitle: Raw material, distillation and cask decide a spirit’s character
slides.1.title: Distillation
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Principle
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Alcohol boils at a lower temperature than water, so heating a fermented liquid gives vapour richer in alcohol, which condenses into spirit; distillation only concentrates, so the raw material’s flavour must already be in the wash
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Pot still
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Batch distillation, usually twice (or three times); retains more flavour compounds (congeners) for a heavier body, e.g. Scotch single malt, Cognac
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Column still
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Runs continuously and efficiently, reaching very high strength with a lighter, cleaner style, e.g. vodka, grain whisky, most light rums
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Heads, hearts and tails
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The first heads contain harsh volatiles and the final tails oily, heavy compounds; the distiller keeps the hearts, and where to cut is a style decision
slides.1.content: Pot stills keep flavour, column stills pursue purity: the first fork in every spirit style.
slides.2.title: Maturation and labelling
slides.2.highlights.0.title: What oak does
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Casks add colour and flavours such as vanilla and spice (extraction), the char layer absorbs harsh compounds (subtraction), traces of oxygen soften the spirit (oxidation), and water and alcohol evaporate (the angels’ share)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Effect of climate
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Maturation is much faster in hot places (Caribbean rum, Kentucky warehouses) and slower in cool, damp Scotland, so age statements from different places cannot be compared directly
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Age statements
slides.2.highlights.2.content: An age statement on whisky and similar spirits gives the age of the youngest component in the blend; colour may be adjusted with caramel, so it cannot be used alone to judge age
slides.2.content: The same “12 years” means very different maturity in Scotland and in the tropics.
